subject: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finwise.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO recap + next steps for load test

Hi Sam - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led load test scheduled and make sure we validate the performance/SLOs you care about.

Recap (from your requirements):
- Latency targets: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 200ms (in-region) for non-streaming generation.
- Streaming: client-side streaming required for long responses; target end-to-end P95 for first-token < 300ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: expected peak 600 reqs/s with ~1200 concurrent streaming sessions during peak batch window.
- Token mix: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 30% long (>=512 tokens).

Next steps / asks from FinWise:
1) Share your k6/Locust scripts (or we can use ours and you can validate).
2) Provide a test account or API key we can provision in our staging environment (or we will provide a test token).
3) Confirm a 2-hour test window (preferred: Wed 2027-04-02 10:00-12:00 PT).
4) Provide IPs to allowlist on your firewall for our test runners, or let us know if you will run the load from your side.
5) Ramp plan: a simple step-ramp (5m ramp to 25%, 10m to 50%, 15m to 100% sustain) is fine - attach any variations you prefer.

Logan (cc'd) will own the test run configuration and can provide Redwood's IPs and temporary capacity plan. Rishi will monitor latency/kv cache behavior and watch for regressions.

Attachments: redwood_loadtest_checklist.pdf (internal checklist)

Thanks - if you confirm the window we will lock in run and send formal instructions + allowlist template.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap + next steps for load test

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. Priya and I reviewed internally and we can run the customer-led load test on our side with Redwood observing and providing IPs. Confirming items below:

1) Test window: Wed 2027-04-02 10:00-12:00 PT works for us.
2) We will attach our k6 script and ramp plan in this thread (finwise_k6_load_v1.js, finwise_ramp_plan.xlsx).
3) Test account: we will create a scoped test API key with limited scope and send the token via a secure channel prior to the run (we will not paste the token in email).
4) IP allowlist: we need the list of Redwood test agent IPs and outbound ports so our infra team can whitelist.
5) Concurrency question: we can provision up to 1500 concurrent sessions during the window if needed - can Redwood handle burst capacity if we hit that?

Attaching: finwise_k6_load_v1.js, finwise_ramp_plan.xlsx

Thanks - Sam
Sam Patel | Engineering Manager, Platform
FinWise (sam.patel@finwise.com)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap + next steps for load test

Sam - appreciate the quick reply. A few practicals from the Redwood side:

1) IPs to allowlist: 34.201.45.12, 34.201.45.13, 34.201.45.14 (these are our test runner egress addresses). Please allow outbound TCP ports 443 and 8443. We'll confirm if additional addresses are needed the day before the run.

2) Test account instructions: we prefer a scoped API key with: read/write testing scope, rate-limited to our session window. If you prefer, we can provide a test token from our staging environment instead - let us know which is easier. See attached test_account_instructions.txt for exact header/curl examples.

3) Streaming vs non-streaming: please include both scenarios in your scripts. For streaming tests, ensure clients keep connections open for the duration of the response; include a ~50% streaming fraction to reflect your anticipated workload.

4) Concurrency/provisioning: Redwood can provision burst capacity for this run. For 1500 concurrent sessions we recommend enabling our "burst pool" which we will provision for the window - this requires a short approval from FinWise infra (confirm below) and we will tag the run in our console so you can see real-time metrics.

Attachments: ip_allowlist_template.txt, test_account_instructions.txt

I will monitor the run with Rishi and can hop on a quick call during the window if anything unexpected comes up.

- Logan
Logan Wright | Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai

- Marissa
